description.p: BChat is a calm, modern IRC client with the classic layout: a network tree, a topic bar, the chat and a nick list with status lights. It talks only to the IRC networks you choose.

ul.li: Networks with auto-connect and auto-join, SSL/TLS, SASL, certificate login, NickServ, bouncers and proxies
Passwords kept in your desktop's keyring, never in a settings file
Notification cards for highlights, private messages and friends coming online
File transfers and direct chats, with a File Transfers window
Python scripts, your own right-click menus, and spell check while you type
Daily logs with a window to search them, and seventeen themes
irc:// and ircs:// links open in BChat

description.p: BChat is now available as a Flatpak.

ul.li: Updates come from your software centre, so BChat's own update check is hidden
Start when I log in asks your desktop once for permission
Received files go to your Downloads folder by default
Speech uses your desktop's speech service and its voices
Passwords in your desktop's keyring (GNOME Keyring, KDE Wallet or KeePassXC). If no keyring answers, BChat says so and keeps no passwords at all.
An app menu entry, irc:// and ircs:// links open in BChat, and Start when I log in
/np shares what your music player is playing, /sysinfo shows your distro and kernel, and Speech reads messages aloud with your desktop's voices
Log replay and search read dates the same on every Python version, and a 29 February line no longer trips them
